State funded elections are a necessity for weeding out corruption in this vibrant democracy. But the Budget could not show the way. The Indian economy has been tied in knots. Growth has slowed as a result of demonetization. We find no road map for the nation. I oppose the Budget. 

श्री भैरों प्रसाद मिश्र (बांदा) : माननीय अध्यक्ष जी, हमारे वित्त मंत्री जी ने जो एतिहासिक और देश की कायाकल्प करने वाला बजट पेश किया है, मैं उसके लिए उनको बधाई देता हूं। इसमें ग्रामीण विकास पर विशेष जोर दिया गया है। ‘सबका साथ सबका विकास’ के तहत सभी वर्गों का काफी ध्यान रखा गया है। प्रधान मंत्री आवास योजना के तहत बजट को 20936 करोड़ रुपये से बढ़ाकर 29043 करोड़ रुपये कर दिया गया है जो लगभग 45 प्रतिशत है और इससे वर्ष 2022 तक सभी लोगों के घर का सपना पूरा होगा। 23000 करोड़ रुपये से 1 करोड़ सस्ते मकान बनाने का लक्ष्य रखा गया है जिससे आम आदमी को लाभ होगा।

महिला एवं बाल विकास के बजट में 16580 करोड़ से बढ़ाकर 20755 करोड़ किया गया है। नेशनल हैल्थ मिशन के तहत बजट को 22598 करोड़ रु. से बढ़ाकर 27131 करोड़ रुपये किया गया है। स्वच्छ भारत अभियान के तहत 12800 करोड़ रुपये से बढ़ाकर 16248 करोड़ रुपये किया गया है। नमाम गंगे योजना के तहत 1441 करोड़ रुपये से बढ़ाकर 2250 करोड़ रुपये किया गया है। हरित क्रांति लाने के लिए बजट को 10360 करोड़ रुपये से बढ़ाकर 13741 करोड़ रु. किया गया है। किसानों को 10 लाख रुपये का कृषि ऋण जो एतिहासिक स्तर पर बजट रखा गया है, उससे जरुरतमंद किसानों को कृषि ऋण उपलब्ध हो सकेगा। सबसे बड़ा लाभ जो मध्यम वर्गों को छूट में दिया गया है, 3 लाख रुपये तक की आय को बिल्कुल कर मुक्त कर दिया गया है। जो राहत का स्लैब था, उसे ढ़ाई लाख से पांच लाख रुपये को घटाकर, 10 प्रतिशत से 5 प्रतिशत किया गया है जिससे जो ईमानदार आयकर दाता हैं, उनको लाभ होगा।

रेल सड़क और उड्डयन को एक साथ बढ़ाने पर जोर दिया गया है। जी.एस.टी. को 1 जुलाई से लागू करने के लिए इसमें प्रमुखता दिखाई गई है और प्रोपर्टी और सोने पर आधार वर्ष की गणना 1981 की जगह 2001 करने से आम लोगों को लाभ होगा। मुद्रा योजना के ऋण हेतु 244000 करोड़ रुपये का प्रावधान किया गया है, इससे जरुरतमंद बेरोजगारों को रोजगार मिलने में सुविधा हो सकेगी। ग्रामीण क्षेत्रों में भारत प्रोजेक्ट के तहत 10000 करोड़ रुपये का प्रावधान किया गया है। इसके लिए डिसकॉम स्कीम लागू की गई है जिससे ग्रामीण क्षेत्रों में रहने वाले लोगों को फायदा होगा। बैंकों के व आम नागरिकों के पैसे लेकर भागने वालों के लिए सम्पत्ति जब्त करने का जो कानून बनाया गया है, उससे उन्हें भारत वापस आने पर मजबूर होना पड़ेगा और कानूनी कार्यवाही का सामना करना ही होगा। ऊर्जा क्षेत्र के लिए 35 प्रतिशत से ज्यादा आबंटन करके हर घर को शीघ्र बिजली उपलब्ध कराने की तत्परता दिखाई गई है। राजनीतिक चंदे की लिमिट 2000 रुपये करने से राजनैतिक स्वच्छता आएगी। 1 करोड़ गरीब परिवारों को गरीबी रेखा से ऊपर लाने के लिए मिशन अन्त्योदय योजना लागू की गई है जिसके तहत 2019 तक 50000 गांवों को गरीबी मुक्त बनाने का संकल्प लिया गया है। 648 जिलों में मुद्रा परीक्षण केन्द्र बनाने का जो लक्ष्य रखा गया है, यह बहुत ही स्वागत योग्य कदम है। 

अनुसूचित जाति के कल्याण की योजनाओं में 35 प्रतिशत की वृद्धि की गई है। 38833 करोड़ रुपये से बढ़ाकर 52393 करोड़ रुपया किया गया है। 

मैडम, मैं बुंदेलखंड क्षेत्र का रहने वाला हूं। मैं आपसे एक निवेदन करना चाहता हूं। इस बजट में बुंदेलखंड क्षेत्र के लिए विशेष तौर से हमारे यहां अन्ना प्रथा की समस्या है। उन्होंने मनरेगा के लिए बजट 48000 करोड़ रुपये बढ़ाया है, लेकिन अन्ना प्रथा की समाप्ति के लिए जिसमें जानवरों को खुला छोड़ दिया जाता है, मेरा निवेदन है कि जानवरों के लिए भी आश्रय गृह बनाने का इसमें प्रावधान किया जाए। दूसरे, मेरा निवेदन है कि रेल के दोहरीकरण के लिए 3500 करोड़ रुपये के प्रावधान की फाइल- झांसी से मिर्जापुर और बांदा से कानपुर तक की दोहरीकरण की फाइल नीति आयोग के पास विचाराधीन है। उसको शीघ्र मंजूर करके शुरू कराया जाये, यह मेरा निवेदन है। बुंदेलखंड विकास बोर्ड या परिषद का गठन किया जाये, जिससे बुंदेलखंड की बदहाली दूर हो सके। इस वर्ष प्रधानमंत्री सिंचाई योजना में सभी जिले शामिल किये जाये। 

मैं दो बातें कह कर अपनी बात समाप्त करूंगा। लोकतांत्रिक सेनानियों को रेल किराये में छूट दी जाये, जिस तरह से सांसद और विधायक को फ्री पास दिया जाता है एवं अन्य लोगों को यह दिया जाता है, उनको भी यह सुविधा दी जाये। मैं इस बजट में इसकी मांग करता हूं। बुंदेलखंड के पलायन को रोकने के लिए क्षेत्र में उद्योग लगाये जायें। यहां वर्गा ग्लास फैक्ट्री है, मेरे यहां कताई मिल है, सिल्का सैंड ग्रेनाइट बड़ी मात्रा में पाई जाती है।...(व्यवधान)

माननीय अध्यक्ष : कृपया आप बैठ जाइए। आपने अपनी बात कह दी है।

*SHRI P.K. BIJU (ALATHUR): The big focus in Finance Minister Arun Jaitley's budget appears to be to further the growth agenda for rural and infrastructure development and push for job creation. Alongside, the budget has attempted to bring in some relief to the middle-class, boost affordable housing, and promote digitisation in the economy. Through the announcement of budget, the government is pretending pro-poor. But what is the reality? Like all union budgets, the budget 2017 also is long on promises but hides the real dynamics.

At a time when the common people of India are reeling under the disastrous impacts of demonetisation, the Finance Minister has come out with a contractionary budget which is likely to greatly exacerbate suffering of the working people. In his speech, Arun Jaitley defended demonetisation, saying it would increase revenues by forcing people to declare untaxed wealth, but conceded that it had hit the economy. On Tuesday, the government lowered its growth forecast for the year ending in March 2017 to 7.1 per cent, down from 7.6 per cent in the previous year.

The budget 2017 is simply misleading and directionless and the Government has shifted it to avoid presenting the ill effects of demonetization. It is misleading because it is based on the data of just six months. The data from the third fisacal quarter, where the ill-effects of demonetisation will be visible, is not included in it. The budget, and all the rosy figures the Finance Minister is showing, is based on data prior to November 8, when demonetisation was announced. The estimates and projections are thus wrong.

The Finance Minister repeatedly talked about doubling incomes of farmers. This does not reflect any increase in outlays for agriculture. The allocation for Department of Agriculture, Cooperation and Farmers' Welfare has fallen from 1.98 per cent of total expenditure in 2016-17 (RE) to 1.95 per cent of total budgetary outlay in 2017-18. There is no increase even in the major flagship programmes of the Government, and the Government seems to be relying only on the banking system for achieving this. Despite the major statements made by the Finance Minister, actual spending on agriculture has hardly increased. Most of the increase is a sleight of hand because an interest subsidy that was provided by the Finance Ministry has been moved into the Agriculture Ministry's budget, 15,000 crores of it. The full increase in spending on agriculture has only increased by 0.01 % of GDP, that is to say, it has gone from 0.99% of GDP to 0.1% of GDP. It's a tiny increase. Taxes forgone due to budgetary measures have gone up by about Rs. 30 thousand crores and are put at 2.1 per cent of GDP. It clearly shows the pro-capitalist leaning of the Government. On the other side, the budget, which boasts of a farmer's budget, is escaping from the sordid realities of the Indian agrarian sector. The Government is showing a blind eye towards the average of 52 a day farmer suicides in all India. As per the economic survey 2016, around 48.9 per cent of the population is solely dependent on agriculture for their livelihood. It is the biggest contributor of country's GDP with 17 percent of the total. But the growth of the agriculture is only a staggering 2.2 percent. The nomenclature of Agriculture also includes livestock, forestry and fishery. Considering this fact, the actual growth of the agriculture would be farfetched from the current growth. It is a shame on the Government that except sugarcane, all crops have been showing a negative growth. Growth of rice is -1.6% wheat is -7.6%, pulses is -10.8%, ground nut is -32.2% and only sugar shows a positive growth with 2.7%.

The latest Economic Survey presented clearly shows a deceleration in economic growth, a sharp fall in demand for goods and services, massive job losses, decline in farm incomes, and social disruption in cash-intensive sectors. Demonetisation has resulted in large unutilized industrial capacity, with core industries like automobiles, cement, steel, paper, aluminium and fertilisers having been hardest hit, and massive unemployment. It is travesty that, in such a situation, and despite having 40 million tonnes of public foodstocks, and a comfortable current account deficit and foreign exchange situation, the government wants to pursue contractionary fiscal policies. The proposal to reduce income tax for MSMEs with an annual turnover of under Rs. 50 crores ignores the interconnectedness of the Indian corporate sector, and opens up a new avenue for corporate tax evasion.

This budget has abolished the practice of plan fund and non-plan fund classification. As the Modi Government consigns five-year plans to history, that it would pose an existential threat to the Special Component Plan (SCP) for Scheduled Castes (SCs) and Tribal Sub Plan (TSP) for Scheduled Tribes (STs). It is disheartening to see the anchoring role of 'plan' in the Budget for determining SCSP and TSP left in a limbo after the removal of the plan and non-plan categories. For previous year allocations, 16.6 % Of the plan budget amounts to Rs. 91,386 crore as due allocation for SCs. This amounts to 4.62% of the total Budget expenditure. Similarly, due allocation for STs amounts to Rs. 47,276 crore, which equals to 2.32% of the total Budget expenditure. Taking this as the benchmark for allocation, in the 2017-18 Budget due allocations for SCs stood at 4.63% and STs at 2.39% of the total budgeted expenditure, which is Rs. 96,638 crore for SCSP and Rs. 49,992 crore for the TSP. Analysis of the allocations under the SCSP the TSP reveals a recurring trend of under-allocation in 2017-18, wherein the SCSP comprises only 2.5% and the TSP only 1.53% of total allocations, which is not even the half of the mandated amount. That means, out of the total 21.47 lakh crore Union Budget 2017-18, a total of Rs. 44,246 crore for SCs and Rs. 18,073 crore for STs has been denied by the central government. I have raised this issue in the Parliament and argued for a special session on this issue.

Rural credit is another important sector neglected by the budget. The actual beneficiaries are not farmers but the corporates. In 2015, the Government had merged the direct and indirect agriculture in to one under the priority sector lending. Direct agriculture refers to individual famers or groups directly engaged in agriculture and allied activities. The indirect sector is mainly engaged by the corporates. Now the banks can meet their entire agriculture lending target-18 percent of their net loans by lending it to corporates. That is why, even after disbursing of 2 lakh crore by the NABARD in the last financial year, it was not reflected in the agriculture growth. The budget is chanting farmer frequently and helping the corporates by taking name of the poor. 

The Finance Minister appears to be addressing the recession by creating a housing bubble. The inclusion of affordable housing in the definition of infrastructure will make it exempt from stringent provisions of land acquisition, extend priority sector lending at subsidised rates to provide cheap land and credit to builders, and include larger houses under the affordable housing are all aimed in that direction. The reduction in capital gains liability by bringing the base year forward to 2001 from 1981 is aimed at giving windfall gains to real estate speculators and builders.

MGNREGA is one of the largest poverty alleviation programmes of the government. Despite the deflationary conditions and in contrast with loud claims made by the FM in his speech, the numbers in the budget document show that there is no substantial increase in allocation for MGNREGA over what is estimated to have been spent last year. Last year, it was 47.4 thousand crores and this year there is only a marginal increase of 48 thousand crores, that means only a meager 501 thousand crore increase. At the present time, the dues pending for MNREGA by various states is more than Rs. 8000 crores. In my state Kerala, it amounts to more than Rs. 300 crores. The meager increase cannot fullfill the objective of MNREGA, especially in the post demonetization scenario that has badly hit the employment prospectus of the rural poor.

Budget 2017-18 has been very disappointing for the education sector. A higher allocation of resources for school education from pre-school to secondary education was expected. But after a year of long waiting, school education has been totally neglected in the budget. The budget has ignored the effective implementation of the Right to Education Act (RTE) and a meager increase in the Sarva Shiksha Abhiyan (SSA) budget- by Rs. 1,000 crores- is not going to help in any way to implement the RTE Act meaningfully. School education for children aged between six to 14 years is a fundamental right in India. However, from 2010, after the Act was passed, it has faced severe challenges in proper implementation.

Two deadlines of 2013 and 2015 have elapsed and the concern of non-implementation due to inadequate resources continues to remain a major barrier to universal school education. In this Budget, Finance Minister Arun Jaitley has increased only Rs. 1,305 crores for the national Education Mission which comprise of the SSA, the Rashtriya Madhayamik Shiksha Abhiyan (RMSA) along with teacher training and adult education. It shows that the Government does not prioritise primary and secondary education along with teacher training and development, which form an essential component for achieving quality education. A nominal increase of Rs. 300 crores in mid-day meals is also totally insufficient to combat malnutrition among the millions of school-going children.

Unfortunately, after six years of implementation of the Act, only 9.5% schools have been made RTE compliant across the country. It has been well documented that millions of children are still out of school and that thousands of additional schools are yet to be built while lakhs of teachers are yet to be recruited and trained. Low allocation is hampering the quality of education in government schools, which have a teacher vacancy of more than 5 lakh, and at least 6.4 lakh teachers are untrained. Ten percent of the schools are single teacher schools, 30% of the schools are without functional toilets for girls and 20% of the schools still lack safe drinking water.

In gender terms, this budget disappoints because in real terms there is decline in the spending of the women and child ministry. The ICDS spending has declined even in nominal terms. The allocation for this year is Rs. 14,000 crore but last year they spent Rs. 15,394 crore. So, that means that the anganwadi system will be really very badly affected and state governments will have to spend more.

First time in the history of the budget, a 93-year-old tradition of a separate Railway Budget has been scrapped by the Center. There are reasons to believe that the Narendra Modi Government's decision to merge the railway budget with the general budget is part of the Government's larger strategy to privatise Railways, India's largest public carrier. The railway is critical since its services complement many other sectors and the broader economy. It commutes workers with less charge, transport goods and food materials. Scrapping Railway budget restricts the organisation's capacity and finally leads to the privatisation of services. Now, the railway service charges are paralleling flight charges. The passenger and freight fares are sky rocketing every year. Why the Government has failed to understand that, even a small hike in passenger and freight fares will have multiple impacts on the economy of our country. Why the government fails to understand that the freight hike is the major reason for the sky rocketing inflation food price? Increase in freight charges in commodities like coal, cement, steel would add to the cost of production. Inflation of price of the cement and steel would further increase the cost of construction. It will badly affect the dream of the homeless to own a roof over their head.

The frequent railway accidents in country is shocking and hundreds of people have lost their lives. Thousands of vacancies still remain vacant in the Railways. Instead of filling the vacancies, the railway is outsourcing its services to private companies that are not accountable. The safety and security of the Indian Railway is really condemnable.

It is also highly condemnable the regional discrimination of the central government with a vengeance. Kerala has been a historically neglected region for railway. Kerala is a world-renowned tourist destination. It is also well known for its beautiful religious destinations. But the insufficient funds earmarked for new lanes, gauge conversion, doubling of lanes and electrification act as a major impediment in the railway development of the stare.

In order to boost the Pilgrim tourism, a new service should be started between Guruvayur and Mookambika. Gauge conversion of Dindigal-Rameswaram is over and it is proposed to start a new train connecting Guruvayoor-Rameswaram via Palakkadu, Dindigal, Madurai. This will lift up the pilgrim tourism in the South India and will have a huge revenue-generation step for the railway.

The long-standing demand of the state for more trains from important cities, a separate railway zone, track doubling and electrification, development of Adarsh stations at Vallatholnagar and Vadakkancherry, has not been met. The demand for Railway Over Bridges, at Kollengode-Oottara, Muthalamada under Palakkadu division, Enkekkadu, Pottore, Akamala, Mulloorkkara under Thiruvananthapuram division, subway at Peruvambu are also neglected. Kerala has acquired 235 acres of land for the Kanjikkode factory. Even after laying the foundation stone five years back, nothing has been done on that land.

The cooperative bank, which is the main source of banking for the rural poor are hit badly by the demonetization. In Kerala, where cooperative movement is a great success, the demonetization exercise has literally broke the poor man's banking system. Through demolishing cooperative banks and subverting the noble spirit behind the cooperative movement, the government is helping the new generation private banks and crumbling the rural economy.

To sum up, this budget not only ignores but also imposes further burdens on the people in the wake of demonetisation and widespread deflationary conditions. With these words I conclude. 

SHRI PREM DAS RAI (SIKKIM): Respected Speaker Madam, I rise to support the Budget placed by the NDA Government in this august House by the hon. Finance Minister on 1st of February this year. I also welcome, on behalf of my Party, the Sikkim Democratic Front, the change in dates. I think the move to get it further ahead is a thoughtful one and I congratulate the Prime Minister.

The Budget has been modestly increased over the revised Budget of the last year by less than seven per cent, perhaps representing the inflation rate that is currently on. However, it is a good Budget in my view because of the prevailing international and national sentiments in a depressed economic situation all over the world. 

I am happy to note the increase in the health Budget under the NHM by over 21 per cent. This infusion is required if India must tackle the massive issues of maternal and child health. Furthermore, new forms of contraceptives are also being thought of. This augurs well for our family planning and especially spacing program which now includes the injectable contraceptives as well. I would request the Government to set up a Commission to oversee the work of family planning in our country and monitor the progress actively. This is the need of the hour. 

Coming to my State of Sikkim, I would like to say that it has suffered immensely from the inverted award of the 14th Finance Commission. This has been brought to the notice of the Ministry earlier and they are seized of the issues. However, we have not received any respite and hence through this House I would like to make a request to the Ministry to make good the loss of over Rs. 1,500 crore annually for the last two fiscals. 

Sikkim is doing well in all-round development but the fiscal shock that we have received has been rude and very debilitating. Hence, many of our stalled projects need to be restarted and benefits to the people of Sikkim restored. We are hopeful that this will be the case. 

I do want to state that we tied over the demonetisation issues rather well, thanks to all-round support especially to the State Bank of Sikkim. This is a Bank which is the treasury to the State Government and has been a legacy of the erstwhile Kingdom. Hence, it falls under the 371F provisions. I am glad that the Home Ministry has helped us in this regard. We recognise this good gesture.

We now await the Bill in Parliament which will ensure reservation of seats to our Scheduled Tribe communities, namely the Limboo and Tamangs whilst at the same time expanding the Assembly strength to 40 with allocation of five seats to the communities. The Bhutia Lepcha communities will continue to enjoy 12 seats reservation. 

With these words, I support the Budget. Jai Hind.

SHRI C.K. SANGMA (TURA): I too rise to support the Budget that has been presented. Keeping in mind the situation that is prevailing in the country and in the world as a whole, it is a very balanced Budget. Keeping the variables that we face, I think, the Budget has been done very well. 

At the same time, I too support the entire idea of bringing forward the Budget. I think the Budget focuses on long-term aspects, like the investment in infrastructure, investment that we are going to put in agriculture, etc. I think it is a long-term based Budget.

Other people have talked a lot about all the other sectors. I would like to come to my region of North-East. In the North-East the budget has gone up by almost 35 per cent, according to the Budget at a Glance, which has increased from Rs.31,422 crore to Rs.42, 499 crore, which is really a welcome move. At the same time, I am very saddened to see that the amount that was given in the 2016-17 budget for the Autonomous District Councils of North East, which had a budget of Rs.1,000 crore, was reduced to Rs.1 crore in the Revised Estimate of 2016-17. 

As you are aware, we do not have the Panchayati Raj in most of the areas; the tribal areas have Autonomous District Councils, and the Government had done a very positive move by giving these funds to the District Councils. Now, by removing this amount, by reducing it from Rs.1,000 crore to Rs.1 crore in 2016-17 will really affect the development prospect. At the same time, the Government had reduced the Budget Estimates for this year for the District Councils from Rs.1,000 to Rs.500 crore. My request to the hon. Finance Minister and his Ministry is that the change that has been made in the Revised Estimates for this year must be brought back to Rs.1,000 crore. At the same time, the budget for this year for the Autonomous District Councils should be increased further. 

As you are aware, the District Councils which are there in Manipur, especially in the Kuki and Naga areas, don’t receive any money or grant from the Government of India. We, luckily as the Sixth Scheduled Area, receive funds. These are elected bodies; these are people elected by the public; and without any funds today, today they are facing huge difficulty. This is one of the main reasons why we are seeing difficulty in the entire North East and the kind of problems that the North East faces. I always believed that if we wanted to have peace in North East Region, we must bring development first. If development comes, peace will follow. Therefore, the Government of India’s policy of Look East, the Act East, and giving more importance to North East is welcome. Our Prime Minister has been very focused on the North-East. I hope this process continues. 

At the same time, the budget allocation for the North East Council also sadly has not increased. It has gone down by Rs.10 crore from Rs.780 crore to Rs.770 crore. I would request the hon. Finance Minister to increase the budget for the North East Council.

You must be aware, Madam, there was a very sad incident where a North East student in Bangalore was beaten up by certain people, the video of which went viral all over. Even today in this country, if our boys and girls and students from North East have to face difficulties like this, I think, it is very sad. Till today no action has been taken regarding that. There was a Bez Baruha Committee which made recommendations to increase the safety of North East people in all the metropolitan cities. Some recommendations have been adopted, many have not. I would urge that some investment be made in this and recommendations be taken up.

Lastly, this is regarding FCRA. The Arch Bishop of Mumbai who has been running more than 200 schools in and around Mumbai areas in Maharashtra have not been receiving funds because the FCRA registration has not been renewed. For this, we had to go, I myself had to go to the Joint Secretary’s and Director’s office only to find out that the manpower in these offices are not enough. Because of 

this, more than 10,000-15,000 students are suffering today. My request to you would be if the Government pays more focus, especially the Ministry of Home Affairs have more manpower in these areas, these kinds of cases can be taken up. 

With these words, I support this Budget. I thank you for giving me this time to speak and participate. 

* DR. A. SAMPATH (ATTINGAL): First of all, I would like to express the pain and anguish of the common people when the Government of India has decided to end the 92 year old practice of a separate Railway Budget. A good precedent is gone without any discussion in the House of the People. In a way, this is an insult to the Parliament.

The Parliament is not an instrument of the executive just to get the nod or an organ to set the records right. Our Railway is people's mode of transport. It is neither a luxury nor a vacation. Every day, 12000 train services carrying 1.30 crores of people and having the 4th largest kilometerage in the world-that is our Railway.

After the President's Address, the next important business was Railway Budget. We were provided about a dozen documents and books to enlighten the public regarding the Railways. But, quite surprisingly, this year we received only 2 books for name sake- is it fair?

The budgetary support to the Railways is to be increased because it bears a social cost of more than Rs. 25,000 crores per annum. Of course, just because of the LIC is still in public sector even though it is facing the challenges of neo liberal era. Railways can receive loan to the tune of Rs. 5 Lakh crores for the projects with a gestation period of 30 years. But the General Budget of the GOI for 2017-18 envisages for a disinvestment to the tune of Rs. 72,000 crores. You are not going to fetch pearls, but peanuts by this selling spree. Our economy was able to withstand the cold whirlwind of the global economic crisis since the last 10 years because "we have a different system', I am quoting these words from the speech of the then Finance Minister Dr. Pranab Mukherjee in the Lok Sabha. And I have privilege to say that our Trade Unions and other working class movements were the warriors who protected the PSUs and national wealth, who fought the agents of loot and plunder, who came under the guise of disinvestment and consequent privatisation of the public wealth.

This Budget is the first one after the demonetisation of November 8th 2016. Those who praised the GOI predicted for a Universal Basic Income (UBI) scheme for the poor, to the BPL families. But, it was miraculously absent! Why?

When we discuss this on the February 8th of 2017, it has been in the news, that almost ¼ of the ATMs in the country has gone dry. Is this an agenda item for a "cash less economy?" The Finance Minister does not tell how much of new currency notes were printed and put to circulation since November 8th . He neither says about the amount black, I mean, the illegal money confiscated since demonetisation.

If somebody wants to enjoy by imitating Don Quixote, let him do so, but not at the expense of the people of a great nation. Till now about 140 people have succumbed to death after standing patiently hours and hours in the queue before the ATMs praying for their hard earned money. Sorry to say this, but if the Finance Minister imitates the role of an unscrupulous doctor who says, "the operation was successful, but the patient died," in what else Parliamentary words shall we pay homages to those people?

Justice has not been shown in gender Budget. The allocation for the health and family welfare including children is inadequate. Even in the days of severe drought, the GOI has failed to address the problem properly.

Why the Budget is silent on abolishing the double taxation in the name of service tax on the Life Insurance Corporation Policies? Why the General Insurance agents still denied of commission while the firms and companies get it? Increasing the limit of MSMEs to the tune to Rs. 50 crores would help the joint stock companies and not the small scale industries. The Budget did not address the issues of traditional sectors like handloom, coir, cashew, bamboo-mat weaving, potteries, fisheries, etc. We need a separate Ministry of Fisheries.

I would like to express my strong reservations on the tendency of the Government of India to by-pass the supremacy of the Parliament. The role of the various departmentally related Standing committees are being reduced to mere organs to look in to the Demand for Grants, whose recommendations are not at all seriously considered by the Executive.

The Finance Minister is trying to generate a set of numbers for projected revenues that are unlikely to be met. Then they find it as an excuse for reducing certain expenditure below the allocated amounts. The end result is that every succeeding year, the Parliamentary discussions on General Budget as well as discussions on the demands for Grants for various Ministries become a futile exercise. The centralized and secretive manner for the eventual spending below the budgeted amount is not at all a healthy practice for a developing nation like India.

Why is the Government reluctant to raise the tax GDP ratios, our country has one of the lowest compared to different OECD countries. We are making subsidy as if it is a big issue. Compared to the subsidy transfers done by the US farm bill and European common agricultural policy, our transfers to farmers is far less. Does the Budget address the decline in the price of agricultural commodities which is affecting Kerala badly. All admit that there is unprecedented crisis in the agricultural sector and especially in the case of perishables like tomato, etc. But it is the same case with coconut, paddy, rubber, spices, etc. also.

The budget has lost its sanctity. It has become distorted without any vision. It is once again a blatant attack on the poor and the oppressed. Why the NPAs are mounting up? Who are the real culprits? It is not the common people but the corporates and the affluent who are able to manage the affairs of the political system, and also to cleverly manipulate. And again, they cry for privatisation also. What a paradox! For what purpose and for whose benefit, the SBT is going to be merged with the SBI. SBT has never come with the begging bowl before the Union Government. It is the prime property of the State of Kerala. It is the money and the wealth of the people of Kerala.

The Finance Minister tries in vain to draw a rosy picture. When 27% of 130 crores of people still remaining illiterate and with largest number of women and children of stunted growth in the whole world, situation in various parts of our country is worse than that of Subsaharan region.

I appeal to the GOI to have a self introspection. Find out your own faults. Take the Parliament into confidence. Let there be discussions and criticisms. Accept the opinions of opposition also, if you can. The GOI has to take helpful measures to strengthen the co-operative sector, including co-operative banks and primary credit societies. They are people's movements which encourage financial stability to the households and small farmers as well as merchants. It is good for financial decentralisation also.

The digital slogan is not bearing fruits. In a country with only 53% of broadband connectivity in the urban areas and a meager 9% in rural areas, the digital divide may deepen economic disparities. In the information and communication Technology Development Index, India ranks a poor 138 out of the 175 countries as per the data of ITU. The Fletcher School at Tufts University has created a Digital Evolution Index of 50 countries and India ranks a lowly 42. According to world bank, 97% of total number of transactions in India is by cash. But we experience severe shortage of currency notes of the denominations of Rs. 10,20,50 and 100. 

The unorganised workers, informal retail traders and street vendors have been forgotten in this Budget also. 

If we want to know the real ingredients of the Budget, we have to go to the appendices and don't believe the speech which hides the facts. Why there was no mention about any road map of filling up of one million vacancies under various Government Departments, PSUs, autonomous bodies, defence, Paramilitary and banks, etc? Social Justice has become forgotten agenda, I fear.

This is a Budget to appease the rich, accentuating the problems of unemployment and rising inequality.

If we implement Adhaar Card, will each and every Indian be able to receive the "promised Sum" of Rs/-15Lakhs in their respective bank accounts? Many of the Budget proposals are detrimental to the economic growth of states like Kerala. Justice is not shown to the five million Indians working abroad and the millions of poor farmers, many of them in the path of committing suicide.

माननीय अध्यक्ष : चिंतामणि मालवीय जी, अब आप बोलिए। आपके पास तीन मिनट हैं। 

प्रो. चिंतामणि मालवीय (उज्जैन) : अध्यक्ष महोदया, मैं आपका धन्यवाद करता हूँ कि आपने मुझे इस युगांतकारी बजट पर बोलने का अवसर दिया। यह बजट हमें बताता है कि यह देश सक्षम और समर्थ हाथों में है। देश बदल रहा है और आगे बढ़ रहा है। 

महोदया, चूँकि समय कम है, इसलिए मैं यह नहीं कहूँगा कि मध्यम वर्ग की आय पर टैक्स कम हुआ है, उस पर 12,500 रुपए की कमी की गई है। न ही मैं यह कहूँगा कि जो मुद्रस्फीति 10 प्रतिशत से ज्यादा थी, वह आज तीन 3 प्रतिशत रह गई है। मैं यह भी नहीं कहूँगा कि हमारा विदेशी मुद्रा का भंडार 359 अरब डॉलर है।

माननीय अध्यक्ष : ऐसा कह-कह कर आप सब कह देंगे। 

प्रो. चिंतामणि मालवीय : अध्यक्ष महोदया, यह भी कहने की आवश्यकता नहीं है कि हमारी जी.डी.पी. आज 7.6 प्रतिशत के उच्चतम स्तर पर है। लेकिन मैं यह जरूर कहना चाहूँगा कि भारत की जो सामरिक शक्ति है, उसके महत्व को जानते हुए हमारे प्रधान मंत्री और हमारी सरकार ने 10 प्रतिशत बजट बढ़ाया है। पिछली सरकारों में हमारा सामरिक वातावरण खराब हो गया था। वर्ष 1984-85 में बोफोर्स नाम की जो बदनाम तोपें खरीदी गई थीं, उनके बाद से कभी तोपें नहीं खरीदी गईं। हमारे मिग विमान हवा में उड़ते हुए ताबूत बन गए थे। अब सक्षम हाथों ने उस खराब सामरिक स्थिति को संभाला है और अंतरराष्ट्रीय परिदृश्य में हम आगे बढ़ने लगे हैं। हम आज बड़े और विकसित देशों के साथ कंपीट करने लगे हैं। 

अध्यक्ष महोदया, मैं यह भी नहीं कहूँगा कि इंफ्रास्ट्रक्चर के क्षेत्र में 2,41,000 रुपए का बजट दिया गया है। मैं सीधे उन बातों पर आना चाहूँगा, जिन पर काँग्रेस के राजकुँवर ने कहा था कि इस बजट में युवाओं, गरीबों और महिलाओं के लिए कुछ नहीं है। उनका कहना था कि, उन्हें लग रहा था यह बजट आतिशबाजी करेगा, लेकिन यह तो गीला बारूद निकला। मैं यह कहना चाहूँगा कि वस्तुतः खुद कांग्रेस आज देश की मौजूदा राजनीतिक परिस्थितियों में बुझी हुई बारूद की तरह हो गई है, जो इतने र्स्पाकिंग बजट को देख नहीं पा रही है। 

अध्यक्ष महोदया, सामान्यतः यह आरोप लगाया जाता है कि यह सरकार सरमायदारों और उद्योगपतियों की सरकार है। इस सरकार पर सूट-बूट की सरकार होने के भी आरोप लगे। इस संबंध में मैं यह कहना चाहूँगा कि यह बजट गरीबों और किसानों के लिए समर्पित है। 

अध्यक्ष महोदया, कई बार जब हमारे घरों में छिपकली आ जाती है, तो वह अक्सर कीट-पतंगे खाकर दीवार पर लगी हुई गांधी जी की तस्वीर के पीछे छिप जाती है। हमारे यहाँ जो खादी पहनते हैं, उन्होंने ही देश में 20 लाख करोड़ रुपए के घोटाले किए। जब एक गरीब का बच्चा इस देश का प्रधान मंत्री बना, तो इन्होंने उसको सूट-बूट की सरकार कहने का पाप और अपराध किया है। खादी पहनकर लाखों करोड़ों रुपए का भ्रष्टाचार करने वालों ने हमारे देश के मान और अभिमान, माननीय प्रधान मंत्री जी पर इस तरह के आरोप लगाए हैं। 

अध्यक्ष महोदया, मैं यह कहना चाहूँगा कि मैं “अनुसूचित जाति” वर्ग से आता हूँ। इस वर्ग के लिए जितना इस सरकार ने किया है, वह आज तक के इतिहास में किसी सरकार ने नहीं किया है। कांग्रेस ने हमेशा अनुसूचित जाति के लोगों के वोटों पर अपना अधिकार जमाया है, लेकिन कभी भी उनको विकसित नहीं होने दिया और आगे भी नहीं बढ़ने दिया। “अनुसूचित जाति” वर्ग के विकास के लिए जो बजट पहले 38,333 करोड़ रुपए था, वह आज 52,393 करोड़ रुपए है। इसमें 35 प्रतिशत की उच्चतम वृद्धि की गई है। 

अध्यक्ष महोदया, कांग्रेस सदा अनुसूचित जाति के खिलाफ रही है। बाबा साहेब अंबेडकर का जो तैल चित्र इस सदन की दीर्घा में लगा है, वह भी माननीय अटल जी की सरकार के आने के बाद लगा है। कांग्रेस ने मदर टैरेसा, खान अब्दुल गफ्फार खान, नैल्सन मंडेला जो यहाँ के नहीं थे, उनको भारत रत्न दिया। श्रीमती इंदिरा गांधी को जीवित रहते हुए दिया, लेकिन बाबा साहेब पर कभी कांग्रेस की नजर नहीं गई। बाबा साहेब को भारत रत्न देने का काम केवल माननीय अटल जी की सरकार ने किया है। 

अध्यक्ष महोदया, ये हमेशा अनुसूचित जाति के खिलाफ काम करते आए हैं। भारतीय जनता पार्टी एक मात्र हमारी ऐसी सरकार है, जिसने अनुसूचित जाति के विकास के लिए 52,000 करोड़ रुपए का बजट दिया है। 

अध्यक्ष महोदया, अब मैं “स्टैंड अप” योजना के बारे में बताना चाहूँगा। इस योजना का मतलब है कि बैसाखियों की आवश्यकता नहीं है, अपने पैरों पर खड़े हो जाओ। वे केवल जॉब सीकर थे। उन्हें जॉब प्रोवाइडर बानाने का काम हमारी सरकार ने इस मुद्रा योजना के माध्यम से किया है।

श्रीमती रंजीत रंजन (सुपौल) : अध्यक्ष महोदया, कल किसानों के बारे में जब हम लोग नोटबंदी पर यह कहने का प्रयास कर रहे थे, कि इससे किसानों को बहुत नुकसान हुआ है, तो जेटली साहब ने बहुत ही अच्छे तरीके से यह समझाने की कोशिश की कि आप बेफिक्र रहिए, किसानों पर टैक्स नहीं लगता है । किसानों को नोटबंदी में कोई भी नुकसान नहीं हुआ, उनके पास नोटबंदी का कोई रीजन नहीं था। उनकी राय गलत थी, यह उनका ओपीनियन हो सकता है, क्योंकि किसान निश्चित तौर से डायरेक्ट टैक्स नहीं देते हैं, लेकिन इन्डायरेक्ट टैक्स देते हैं। उनका भी टैक्स लगता है, वह एक समोसा खाने जाते हैं, एक धोती खरीदने जाते हैं, एक कुर्ता खरीदने जाते हैं, परचून की दुकान से अगर सामान लेते हैं तो भी किसान को टैक्स भरना पड़ता है। यह कहना कि नोटबंदी का उस पर असर नहीं हुआ, जो भी उसके पास नोट थे, उन नोटों को भी बैंक में जमा करना पड़ा था। किसान को आपने कोई छूट नहीं दी थी। उस वक्त किसान को अपना धान बेचना था, गेहूँ को उपजाना था, जिसके लिए उनको खाद और यूरिया नहीं मिल पायी, क्योंकि उनके पास पैसे नहीं थे। मार्केट उनको उधार नहीं दे पा रहा था, क्योंकि उनके पास भी माल उठाने के लिए पैसे नहीं थे। आपकी पार्टी की अजीब परंपरा है कि एक तरफ तो आप कहते हैं कि हम 10 लाख करोड़ रुपए किसान के कर्ज के लिए दे रहे हैं, लेकिन किसान कर्ज कैसे चुकाएगा, इसके बारे में आपके बजट में कोई चर्चा नहीं है। यू.पी. में … * दहाड़-दहाड़ कर कह रहे हैं कि यू.पी. के किसानों का कर्ज चुनाव के तुरंत बाद ही माफ कर देगे।

श्री चंदूलाल साहू (महासमन्द) : अध्यक्ष महोदया, आपने मुझे बजट पर बोलने का अवसर दिया, इसके लिए मैं आपको बहुत-बहुत धन्यवाद देना चाहता हूं। यह बजट सर्वस्पर्शी है, संतुलित है और देश के लिए विकासोन्मुखी है। इसलिए मैं इस बजट का समर्थन करता हूं। महात्मा गांधी जी ने कहा है कि यदि आप पहला कदम बढ़ाते हैं तो उस गरीब व्यक्ति का चेहरा याद रखना, अगर आपके कदम से उस गरीब व्यक्ति के चेहरे पर खुशी आ जाए, तब समझो कि आपका कदम सही है। ऐसे सही कदम उठाने वाले हमारे देश के प्रधान मंत्री, श्री नरेन्द्र मोदी जी हैं, जिन्होंने गरीबों के आंसू पोंछने के लिए, गरीबों के विकास के लिए और गरीबों के भोजन आदि की व्यवस्था करने के लिए यह बजट प्रस्तुत किया है। पचास हजार गांवों के एक करोड़ गरीब परिवारों को गरीबी से मुक्त करने की जो योजना है, निश्चित रुप से यह स्वागत योग्य है। 

वर्ष 1971 में गरीबी हटाओ, देश बचाओ का नारा लगाया गया था, लेकिन गरीबों के कल्याण और उनके उत्थान के लिए कोई कार्य नहीं किया गया। मैं समझता हूं कि माननीय नरेन्द्र मोदी जी ने इसके लिए बहुत अच्छा कदम उठाया है। इसके पहले महात्मा गांधी का नाम लेकर बहुत से लोग वोट बैंक की राजनीति करते रहे, लेकिन हमने महात्मा गांधी के नाम पर कभी राजनीति नहीं की, बल्कि उनके आदर्शों को चरितार्थ करने और उन्हें धरातल पर उतारने के लिए प्रयास किया गया है। इस क्रम में जो स्वच्छ भारत अभियान चलाया गया है, निश्चित रुप से इससे गांवों की वे महिलाएं, जो वास्तव में बड़ी शर्म के साथ खुले में शौच आदि के लिए जाती थीं, आज स्वच्छता अभियान के अंतर्गत शासन के और स्वयं के पैसे लगाकर शौचालयों का निर्माण किया जा रहा है। निश्चित रूप से यह भी एक सराहनीय कदम है। 

इसके साथ मैं कहना चाहता हूं कि महात्मा गांधी जी को एक विदेशी पत्रकार ने पूछा था कि गांधी जी आप किस प्रकार से आजादी चाहते हैं तो महात्मा गांधी जी ने कहा कि मैं अपने देश के छः लाख गांवों में सुराज चाहता हूं। जब गांवों में सुराज आयेगा तो निश्चित रूप से रामराज्य आ जायेगा। रामराज्य की परिकल्पना करते हुए महात्मा गांधी जी ने जो कहा था, उस पर किसी ने ध्यान नहीं दिया, लेकिन माननीय नरेन्द्र मोदी जी ने सांसद आदर्श ग्राम योजना लागू करके यह निर्देश दिया है कि सभी सांसद आदर्श ग्राम योजना के तहत एक गांव को गोद ले लें और उस गांव का समुचित विकास करें, ताकि उसे देखकर अन्य गांवों के लोग भी उसे एक आइडियल के रूप में स्वीकार करके अपना विकास करें। लोग कहते हैं कि भारतीय जनता पार्टी के लोग महात्मा गांधी को नहीं मानते, लेकिन मैं कहना चाहता हूं कि इस बजट में महात्मा गांधी के सिद्धांत को पूरा करने का प्रयास किया गया है। 

महोदया, हमारा देश गांवों का देश है और जब तक गांवों का विकास नहीं होगा, तब तक देश का विकास नहीं हो सकता। हमारे गांवों की संस्कृति तालाबों की संस्कृति रही है। भारत देश में एक समय 14 करोड़ तालाब थे, वे तालाब घटते-घटते आज 80 लाख रह गये हैं। लेकिन माननीय नरेन्द्र मोदी जी के द्वारा इस बजट के माध्यम से दस लाख तालाबों के निर्माण की जो व्यवस्था की गई है, यह एक सराहनीय कदम है। एक गांव के लिए तालाब सब कुछ है। पहले लोग तालाबों का पानी पीते थे। मैं भी गांव से आता हूं, जब हम आयु में छोटे थे तो तालाब में ही नहाते थे, तालाब का पानी पीते थे और तालाब के पानी का बहुत सदुपयोग किया जाता था। 

इसके अलावा मैं कहना चाहता हूं कि उज्ज्वला गैस योजना के तहत गरीब परिवारों की माताएं, बहनें कभी कल्पना नहीं कर सकती थीं कि हमारे पास भी गैस सिलेंडर होगा। लेकिन सरकार ने एक कदम आगे बढ़कर उन्हें चूल्हा देने की व्यवस्था की है। सरकार ने उज्ज्वला योजना लागू करके गरीब परिवार का जो सपना था कि मेरे घर में भी गैस कनेक्शन हो, वह पूरा हो रहा है। इसके साथ ही साथ जंगलों को भी बचाने का प्रयास किया गया है। आज जंगल पर्यावरण सुधार के लिए बहुत आवश्यक हैं।
